gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Popular Science (Stan Horaczek, Feb 11, 2026) used the WOLFBOX MegaVolt 24 Air (4000A, 88.8 Wh, the same specs as ChatGPT's 'JS24AIR' truck pick) to take an SUV tire from 25 to 35 psi in about a minute and to start a diesel F-350 that had been sitting unused. Its only cited lab test, TechGearLab's, is of the smaller MegaVolt16 Air, which needed 3 minutes to add 5 psi to a 275/70R18 F-150 tire and held 51.3 Wh of its claimed 59.2 Wh.
standout_why: Compared against the two TechGearLab pages (ranks 1 and 2, cited). They cover only the MegaVolt16 Air, NOCO AX65, Dewalt DXAEJ14 and Stanley J5C09. They give no inflation times in the roundup, no test of the MegaVolt 24 Air, and nothing on the GOOLOO A3. ChatGPT's 'strong independent test results' line borrows the 16 Air's TechGearLab award, but the 24 Air card it showed for trucks has no test behind it on any page it got. I could not open the cited Popular Mechanics GOOLOO article (WebFetch is blocked there, and curl needed approval I don't have), so I can't rule out that it measures the A3. Ranks 4 to 11 are mostly affiliate roundups and I did not open them. I also checked Bob Vila's Nov 10, 2026 lab roundup, which was not in ChatGPT's results. It tests none of the three candidates.
decides: This confirms, without fully proving, ChatGPT's 'bigger vehicle → 4000A WOLFBOX' advice. A named tester got the 24 Air to start a diesel F-350 and add 10 psi in about a minute. That comes from one hands-on review, not a controlled lab test. The tire size was not given, so it can't be compared with TechGearLab's 16 Air figure. It also shows the GOOLOO A3, ChatGPT's 'best value' pick, has no named measurement I could open. A page could say plainly that the A3 rests on maker claims while both WOLFBOX units have tester figures. TechGearLab's measurement of the 16 Air at 87% of its claimed capacity (51.3 / 59.2 Wh) is a useful reminder that the rated Wh on the box is not what you get.
